claims.statement: These teaching contracts contribute useful typed specifications: claim provenance, explicit loss accounting, admitted observation/transport contexts, independently sound permission projections, witnessed irreflexivity, deterministic replay and measure-relative minima. Their force is conditional on actual carriers, maps and validators, not on a normal-form label.

The anti-skill register and self-panel regeneration ticket explicitly limit finite evidence, distinguish detection from antimorphisms, preserve failed runs and historical panels, and separate live model results from mock behavior. These are useful review policies and proposed repairs; this source reading does not demonstrate their universal enforcement.

The concept curriculum identifies reusable policies: prompt material versus execution occurrence, ancestry versus citation, protected-span mutation, finite reachability quarantine, rational comparisons, capacity allocation, candidate-only detector mutation and non-authoritative telemetry. Their names and teaching examples do not supply statistical efficacy, authenticated history or universal enforcement.

All11fully read PCIV notebook code cells run on their retained standard-library toy examples. The forward-taint function also agrees with independent reachability closure on all512three-vertex directed graphs and allthree roots(1536checks). This is bounded algorithm evidence; the other edge-case findings remain and no causal-ancestry or model-performance claim follows.

The 13 fully read EIS notebooks contain 52 reviewed standard-library cells that complete on their fixed toy inputs. Candidate/spec constructors include genuine limited rejection checks, the two-string thymus example computes a real substring match, and the rational-affinity example computes 21/25. This is small teaching-example evidence; constant predictions, simulated falsifiers and absent runtime adapters remain explicit limitations.

The levels add meaningful normative obligations absent from several toy cells: explicit inheritance cycle refusal, exact reserve ties, independently aged usage events, rule-version invalidation versus OR reachability, and a clearly proposed multi-island roadmap. These specifications can guide testable workflows; their header grades do not establish runtime enforcement.

findings.statement: The normal-form indexes misbind several claimed mechanisms to their linked contracts: CDC is row-change evidence, ODNF observer distinguishability, EFNF temporal permission projection, and provenance is semiring query annotation. These are not the claimed causal-derivation, independent-observation, firewall/token-limit or cryptographic lineage contracts. Production/computed/gated metadata also coexists with five verification-absent YAML entries.
findings.recommended_action: Correct the names and scope of each linked contract; separately define and validate the domain adapters and qualify evidence metadata.

findings.statement: Six of the ten local YAML contracts omit certification.loss_ledger_trigger_id, which their adjacent custom meta-schema requires. Both exact schema copies agree. Terminal-route domains and canonical targets do match for all ten.
findings.recommended_action: Add the appropriate declared trigger or null after reviewing the intended policy, and bind metadata to an actual schema-validation result.

findings.statement: SERNF says checking finite generators decides the split identity and that a section preserves base relations, without declaring homomorphism/structure-preservation premises. On additive Z/4Z, u=id and r=(0,1,3,3) pass0/1 but fail at2. Conversely u(x)=x+1 and r(y)=y-1 satisfy the round trip everywhere while u fails to preserve addition.
findings.recommended_action: Check every member of a declared finite carrier, or supply an algebraic presentation and prove the maps are appropriate homomorphisms. State relation preservation separately from a set-theoretic retraction.

findings.statement: The three normative PCIV JSON schemas do not enforce the associated semantic laws. Schema-valid controls allow a100-entry migration quota for one family, arbitrary cochain strings and attenuation weight1 at hop3, and a headstone identifier without its described prefix plus an empty witness. This bounds what schema conformance means; it is not a demonstrated runtime exploit.
findings.recommended_action: Separate shape and semantic validation, add enforceable field constraints, and require bound witnesses/state checks for cross-field and concurrency invariants.

findings.statement: The society definition uses a four-coordinate rational Pareto frontier while its wire schema names only accuracy,cost,robustness. Its written dominance law maximizes every coordinate without a declared transformation for cost. If cost means raw expenditure, equal other scores and higher cost pass that law; if it means utility, that conversion must be explicit.
findings.recommended_action: Declare all coordinates, units and minimize/maximize direction, and align the wire schema with the mathematical comparison. Preserve ties and hold-out evaluation as separate obligations.

findings.statement: Five literal EIS lesson snippets do not enforce adjacent advertised falsifiers. Frozen defaults accept ADMITTED status, the two-signal conjunction accepts a copied true signal, distinct labels on a shared event count as three supports, Fraction converts to float without error, and the signature dataclass accepts empty strings. These are teaching-snippet findings; actual runtime behavior is separately reviewed.
findings.recommended_action: Label incomplete snippets as illustrative, or replace them with runnable examples that exercise a pinned validating implementation and its negative controls.

findings.statement: The concept pages overextend finite or label-based evidence: passing retained near misses does not ensure valid code never triggers, and distinct correlation keys do not establish pairwise-uncorrelated or causally independent observations. The useful properties are finite-panel agreement and cardinality of an admitted equivalence partition.
findings.recommended_action: Name the exact fixture population, justify how keys collapse shared causes, and keep statistical independence/error assumptions explicit.

findings.statement: Several PCIV workbench labels exceed the implemented examples. The PageRank cell is a scalar damped sum without a stationary-equation certificate; the replay cell only checks a supplied payload digest and has no event fold or idempotency; the island cell transfers list entries without crossover or quotas. They are limited teaching examples, not standalone certified workflows.
findings.recommended_action: Rename the demonstrations to their actual computed property, or connect them to a pinned implementation and check the stated certificate/state invariant.

findings.statement: Fresh controls on the reviewed PCIV teaching cells expose five guard/algorithm gaps: a two-edge inheritance cycle is admitted; zero-width insertion inside a protected span succeeds; Pareto zip ignores trailing coordinates and accepts floats; float quotas assign the last seat incorrectly at capacity10^20+1; and an invalid island target loses a genome before raising. These findings apply to the miniature notebook implementations, not automatically to production classes.
findings.recommended_action: Add explicit input/graph/span admission, retain rational remainders, and validate all mutation targets before changing state. Include these controls in the lesson rather than treating a positive printout as a certificate.

findings.statement: All 13 EIS notebook prediction cells assign a literal and compare it with that same literal, independently of the measured state. Several falsifiers manually raise errors or assert preset flags. The overview report permits direct admission assignment, and removing both role-constructor guards in memory still lets every lesson cell complete because the negative test never fails when its expected exception is absent. Queue emission and human signatures are also only narrated/literal in their examples.
findings.recommended_action: Collect a learner prediction before computing the result, compare it with actual output, and exercise a real operation in each negative test with an explicit failure if rejection is absent. Keep toy arithmetic, simulated exceptions and actual runtime evidence distinct.

findings.statement: The PCIV teaching notebook and level specify different algorithms: at capacity10 the written Front/Unmeasured/Baseline tie priority gives [6,3,1], while reverse-index ordering gives [6,2,2]; halfway to a half-life, continuous notebook decay is about0.7071 while the level floor-exponent policy is1. The latter is a policy mismatch, not proof that either decay choice is intrinsically incorrect.
findings.recommended_action: Declare the intended tie priority and decay convention once, and make teaching examples check intermediate boundaries and exact ties against that policy.

findings.statement: The identity level says changes always yield distinct finite digests, and the catalog says UUIDv5 plus payload hashes guarantee zero duplicate provider calls. A finite hash is not an injective map on arbitrary messages; collision resistance is a security assumption. At-most-once provider effects also require an actual crash/retry/idempotency protocol beyond content naming.
findings.recommended_action: Qualify hash guarantees and state the transaction/idempotency assumptions. Keep content equality, recorded custody and external side-effect counts separate.
